question: How warm does handwashing water need to be?
answer: Handwashing water must be warm enough to meet the minimum temperature required by the applicable code.  The 2022 edition of the FDA Food Code specifies that a hand‑washing sink must provide water at a temperature of at least 85 °F (29.4 °C) through a mixing valve or combination faucet (FDA Food Code §5‑202.12, “Water temperature at handwashing sinks”, “at least 85°F (29.4°C)”).  Under the earlier 2017 edition of the FDA Food Code the same requirement was at least 100 °F (38 °C) (FDA Food Code 2017 §5‑202.12, “Water temperature at handwashing sinks”, “at least 100°F (38°C)”).  The Hawaii health‑authority rule does not impose any minimum temperature; hot water is optional and the state rule is the one enforced in Hawaii (Hawaii HAR §11‑50‑61, “No minimum water temperature”, “The Hawaii rule does not set a minimum water temperature”).  Therefore, the governing temperature is 85 °F where the current FDA Food Code is adopted, but in Hawaii the state rule applies and has no minimum temperature requirement.

passages.doc: FDA Food Code §5-202.12 — Handwashing Sink Requirements
passages.heading: Water temperature at handwashing sinks
passages.text:
Water temperature at handwashing sinks
A handwashing sink must be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at
least 85°F (29.4°C) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. A steam
mixing valve may not be used at a handwashing sink, because steam valves are
hard to control and can scald.

passages.doc: FDA Food Code 2017 §5-202.12 — Handwashing Sink Requirements
passages.heading: Water temperature at handwashing sinks
passages.text:
Water temperature at handwashing sinks
Under the 2017 edition, a handwashing sink must be equipped to provide
water at a temperature of at least 100°F (38°C) through a mixing valve or
combination faucet. The 2022 edition later lowered this minimum to 85°F.
A steam mixing valve may not be used at a handwashing sink.

passages.heading: No minimum water temperature
passages.text:
No minimum water temperature
must provide a flow of water for at least
fifteen seconds without the need to reactivate the faucet, and faucets must
provide a sufficient flow of water to permit proper washing and rinsing of
hands.
The Hawaii rule does not set a minimum water temperature for handwashing
sinks: hot water is optional, and the mixing-valve requirement applies only
if hot water is provided. This differs from the FDA model Food Code, which
requires water of at least 85°F at a handwashing sink in its 2022 edition.
In Hawaii establishments, the state rule is the one the health inspector
enforces.

A steam mixing valve may not be used at a handwashing sink.
A self-closing, slow-closing, or metering faucet must provide a flow of

An automatic handwashing facility must be installed in accordance with the
